title: Canary Simulation and Auto-Alert Playbook for Enterprise Cutovers
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook describes a reproducible simulation and automated alert strategy for canary rollouts during enterprise customer cutovers (dedicated and private). It pairs realistic traffic simulation, telemetry checks, and an escalation ladder so Customer Success (CS), SRE, and Platform teams can validate stability before broad traffic migration and capture actionable signals for QBRs.

Goals

- Validate end-to-end request/response correctness for the customer’s integration paths (API, streaming, embedding)
- Detect regressions in inference quality, latency, and cost within the canary window
- Automate high-confidence alerts with clear ownership and rollback criteria
- Produce artifacts for post-cutover QBR and health audits

Scope

Applies to: Hosted -> Dedicated migrations, Dedicated capacity model swaps, Private environment cutovers where Redwood controls the control plane. Excludes large data-only backfills and purely offline batch ingestion.

Key Services and Metrics

- Services referenced in this playbook: redwood-inference-api, routing-proxy, tenant-gateway, telemetry-collector, cost-attribution-worker
- Telemetry surfaces used: request_latency_ms, token_error_rate, model_confidence_degradation (by prompt-set), p99_kvcache_hit_rate, tokens_per_request_avg, infra_gpu_util_pct

Pre-Canary Checklist (owners in parentheses)

1. Configuration and isolation
   - Create a dedicated canary tenant or sub-tenant and pin model_version (Platform).
   - Ensure KV cache warmers are seeded with canonical prefixes for the customer workload (SRE/Platform).
   - Confirm no shared-tenant quotas will throttle canary traffic (Customer Success / Billing).
2. Observability setup
   - Enable the canary dashboard and add the canary tenant filter (SRE).
   - Confirm Prometheus/OTEL queries for p99 latency, error rate, and KV hit rate are returning historical baselines (SRE).
3. Communication
   - Announce window to the customer and internal stakeholders; publish PagerDuty escalation policy (Customer Success).
   - Ensure on-call SRE and Platform engineers are present for the duration (SRE Manager).

Simulation Scenarios

A. Baseline synthetic workload
- Objective: validate steady-state latency and token economics.
- Traffic profile: 200 rps sustained for 10 minutes, steady distribution across short (<=64 tokens), medium (65-512 tokens), and long (>512 tokens) sequences.
- Expected: p95 <= 150ms for short/medium requests; p99 <= 400ms; tokens_per_request_avg within +/-20% of historical baseline.

B. Quality regression injection
- Objective: catch regressions in model outputs (hallucinations or structured output drift).
- Method: run the customer’s canonical prompt-set (50 prompts) and compute similarity/metric (BLEU/ROUGE embed-sim) vs. golden responses.
- Expected: model_confidence_degradation < 3% absolute drop.

C. KV cache pressure scenario
- Objective: exercise cache eviction and fallbacks.
- Method: run high-variance prefix traffic (burst of 1000 unique prefixes over 5 minutes).
- Expected: p99_kvcache_hit_rate decreases but should not cause token_error_rate to rise > 0.5%.

Alerting and Thresholds (table)

| Alert name | Query / Signal | Threshold | Urgency | Owner |
|------------|----------------|-----------|---------|-------|
| Canary: latency spike | query: request_latency_ms{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | p99 > 600ms for 2m | high | SRE-oncall |
| Canary: error rate | query: token_error_rate{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | error_rate > 1% for 1m | high | SRE-oncall |
| Canary: quality drop | script: quality_check(golden_set) | absolute drop >= 3% | high | CS / Applied ML |
| Canary: cost spike | query: tokens_per_request_avg{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | > 30% above baseline for 5m | medium | FinOps / CS |
| Canary: kvcache miss cascade | query: p99_kvcache_hit_rate{tenant=\"canary-123\"} | < 20% for 3m | medium | Platform |

Example Prometheus alert rule (YAML)

groups:
- name: canary.rules
  rules:
  - alert: CanaryHighP99Latency
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{tenant=\"canary-123\"}[1m])) by (le)) > 0.6
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: \"p99 latency for canary-123 > 600ms\"
      runbook: \"/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/canary-deployment-validation\"

Automated Playbook (step-by-step)

1. Start canary window (Customer Success)
   - Notify internal channel #cs-canary-run and the customer via scheduled email.
2. Kick off baseline synthetic workload (SRE)
   - Command: curl -X POST https://ci-sim.redwood.local/simulate -d '{"tenant":"canary-123","profile":"baseline","duration":600}'
3. Monitor the dashboard and watch the top three alerts (latency, error, quality) for the first 10 minutes (SRE / CS).
4. If quality alert triggers, pause canary and run a focused evaluation:
   - Run: python3 tools/quality_eval.py --tenant canary-123 --golden golden_v1.json --output /tmp/canary_eval.json
   - If model_confidence_degradation >= 3% absolute, proceed to Escalation Ladder.
5. If latency or error alerts trigger, triage live traces:
   - Run: otel-cli query --service redwood-inference-api --tenant canary-123 --trace-scan 10m
   - Check KV cache hit rate across nodes via: curl http://telemetry-collector/api/cache/summary?tenant=canary-123
6. Decide: continue, throttle, or rollback. Use the decision matrix below.

Decision Matrix (short)

- Continue: transient alert < 2m, no quality degradation, infra GPU util < 85%
- Throttle: sustained cost spike or p99 latency between 400–600ms with no errors (Platform + CS).
- Rollback: any of the following: token_error_rate > 1% for >1m; quality drop >=3% absolute; p99 latency > 800ms for >2m.

Escalation Ladder

1. SRE-oncall page (immediate)
2. Platform engineer (30 min)
3. Applied ML engineer for quality anomalies (15 min)
4. Customer Success lead + Customer technical contact for customer-impacting degradations (immediate)

Escalation contact table

| Role | PagerDuty | Slack channel | Backup |
|------|----------|---------------|--------|
| SRE-oncall | PD: SRE-CANARY | #sre-oncall | Platform-oncall |
| Platform | PD: PLATFORM | #platform | Eng-infra-manager |
| Applied ML | PD: ML-APPLIED | #applied-ml | ML-lead |

Rollback and Failback Procedure (if rollback chosen)

1. Set routing-policy to legacy (Platform):
   - curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routing -d '{"action":"route","filter":"tenant=canary-123","target":"legacy-pool"}'
2. Disable any automated scaling or batch warmers for the canary (SRE).
3. Notify customer and schedule a follow-up remediation meeting within 48 hours (CS).
4. Capture artifacts: export traces, the canary_eval.json file, dashboard snapshots, and a short incident summary (SRE + CS).

Post-Mortem and QBR Integration

- Required artifact checklist after any canary with a high-severity alert:
  - Incident timeline (UTC)
  - Trace links and top 5 offending traces
  - Quality evaluation report vs golden set
  - Cost delta report (tokens and estimated spend)
  - Action items and owners
- Feed the summary into the next customer QBR under: \"Cutover Learnings\" with recommended SLO adjustments or config changes.

Runbook snippets and queries (copyable)

1) PromQL - p99 latency by route\   histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{tenant=\"canary-123\"}[5m])) by (le, route))

2) SQL - tokens per request (timeseries)\   SELECT bin, avg(tokens_per_request) FROM telemetry.tokens WHERE tenant = 'canary-123' AND ts >= now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY bin ORDER BY bin DESC;

3) Quality check script invocation\   python3 tools/quality_eval.py --tenant canary-123 --profile regression --golden s3://redwood-golden/canary/golden_v1.json --out /tmp/canary_eval.json

Ownership and run cadence

- Canary simulations should be run for all enterprise cutovers and recorded in the Cutover Registry (Customer Success).
- Standard window: 2 hours; extend by mutual agreement with customer and SRE.
- Retrospective: 48–72 hours after any significant alert (CS + SRE + Platform).

Frequently asked questions

Q: What if the customer traffic shape cannot be replicated?
A: Use a hybrid simulation: replay recorded production traces anonymized with adaptive rates. Document difference in the runbook artifacts.

Q: Who owns quality metrics if model outputs degrade?
A: Applied ML triages model-level regressions; CS handles customer communications and rollback decisions.

- [ ] Canary tenant created and pinned to model_version
- [ ] Dashboards populated and filtered for tenant
- [ ] Synthetic baseline simulation executed
- [ ] Golden set evaluation run and recorded
- [ ] PagerDuty escalation policy verified
- [ ] Post-run artifacts uploaded to the customer ticket
